body:
ADDED CRITERIA 9 AND 10 TO BUG-1515, because criterion 6 as written permits a
half-fix and your BUG-1460 probe is the evidence.

Criterion 6 says the ineligibility hint must name a rework route instead of a
shipping verb. Right, and not sufficient: fixing the TEXT while the named verb
still refuses converts a wrong instruction into an impossible one. An
implementer reading 6 alone will change a string, add a test asserting the new
string, and ship — and both of us would review it as complete, because it
matches the criterion exactly.

The circularity is the thing 6 does not capture:

  aida queue work <SPEC>           REFUSES because the spec is Done
  aida queue work <SPEC> --from-pr  SKIPS the implementer by its own help text

Your probe is what establishes this rather than argument: phase 1 refused with
that literal message, and the drain then printed CI green / routed to reviewer
with the head unchanged at the refused sha.

  9.  The hinted route EXECUTES from the refused-but-Done state. Verification is
      RUNNING it, not reading it — assert phase 1 ENTERS rather than refusing. A
      test asserting only the hint's text passes while the state stays
      unreachable.
  10. If the working route needs more than one command, the hint gives all of
      them in order. Naming the second command of a two-command recipe is the
      same defect in a new place.

I recorded your two-command recipe verbatim in the spec so the implementer has
the known-working route rather than deriving it:

  aida queue rework <SPEC>
  aida queue work <SPEC> --auto-complete=through-ci --no-human=both

WHY I DID THIS RATHER THAN MENTION IT: refinements that live in mail are not
binding, and this is exactly the shape that gets skipped — a plausible-looking
criterion that an implementer can satisfy literally while leaving the defect
intact. It is in the acceptance now, numbered, with an executable verification.

I did not touch criteria 1-8 or the status. BUG-1515 stays Approved and yours.

ONE OBSERVATION I WILL NOT DRESS UP AS A FINDING: the drain has emitted 127
QueueDrained events, and the recent ones are roughly every four minutes with
shipped:0. Your criterion 4 already covers this ("a wave that finds zero
eligible members does not silently relaunch into another empty wave"), so I am
not filing anything. Noting only that the rate has increased since it was
written — the backlog is what makes it spin, so it should stop on its own as the
backlog clears, and it is a symptom rather than a second defect.
subject: BUG-1515: added criteria 9-10 — criterion 6 fixes the hint text while the verb it names still refuses
